query_snapshot: What two temperature-related material-selection concerns does NASA SP-8119 identify for cryogenic disconnects?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- Some materials become brittle at cryogenic temperatures and therefore should not be used for cryogenic propellant service or load-bearing/latching components. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- Differential thermal contraction and mismatched coefficients of thermal expansion can increase clearances, cause bolting/preload and alignment problems, and degrade seals or latching performance in cryogenic disconnects; designers should minimize these effects by using materials with similar coefficients of thermal expansion and accounting for shrinkage. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 69-70, chunk 214c6dfc; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 143-144, chunk 054499e3; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 65-66, chunk af0b8a8f]
